Thirty-five generations ago, my ancestors built lives in the high desert of New Mexico. Growing up fishing with my dad and running through the desert with my cousins, I fell in love with New Mexico’s natural wonders and learned that we all have a responsibility to care for our planet.
_Since my childhood, I have seen the impacts of climate change on New Mexico._
That’s why, when I was elected to Congress, I fought to protect sacred lands. As Secretary of the Interior, I helped protect more land and water than any administration in U.S. history while also creating good jobs in clean energy and conservation and cleaning up legacy pollution
**But now all of that progress is at risk.**
Donald Trump and his MAGA allies have worked to gut environmental protections and sell off public lands — all while New Mexico stands on the front lines of the devastating impacts of climate change.
Governors are the first line of defense against the Trump agenda, especially when it comes to standing up against the brazen attacks on our environment. **And as Governor, I will be a fierce defender of our home, but I can’t win this race on my own.**
Republicans have already spent big to stop us because they care more about money than about protecting New Mexico’s families and the beautiful public lands we call home. **[So if you’re with me, friend, I’m personally asking: Will you please chip in $5 today to help power my victory in November so I can protect New Mexico’s land, water, and future?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15440?refcode=jtk1247-fr-nd&t=8&akid=11860%2E400544%2EUb9nOi)**
Thank you for doing your part to protect New Mexico for future generations.

Be Fierce,

— Deb

TX-34, CA-45, CA-13, PA-08, and NM-02. Five districts. One path to a Democratic majority — and it runs through Latino communities in Texas, California, Pennsylvania, and New Mexico.

I have never seen a more corrupt White House than the one that we have right now in Washington.

body:
While we’re busy building the biggest tent in Iowa history, my opponent is forking over millions to spread fear and tell lies on TV.
I just had to make a tough call, Peter, and if I’m being honest, it’s quite a gamble.
For context, my opponent is spending $700,000 a week on TV ads to spread lies about me and my record.
**That’s why I told my team to increase our TV ad budget to make sure we’re competitive on the airwaves.**
While we’re busy building the biggest tent in Iowa history, he’s forking over millions to spread fear and tell lies on TV.
**[I’ll explain what this means for our campaign in a second, but if you’re in a hurry, will you please split $25 ASAP between my campaign and Heartland Patriots so we’re ready to respond to all the baseless partisan attacks in real time?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107804?refcode=em20260822-heartland-patriots-rob-sand&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=1&akid=10827%2E614464%2EffjZo1)**

Still — $700k a week is wall-to-wall coverage. There are a LOT of undecided voters who will see Lahn’s ads, which is why I can’t let his statewide TV lie-a-thon go unchecked.
I’m famously frugal — _bordering on cheap_ — so this was a tough call, but it could mean the difference between losing and winning this election.

Time to reset the clock on Los Angeles finding new ways to get into the national spotlight over the backward decisions made by Democrat leaders.
This week's first example is the city council approving, by a large majority, the removal of homeless enforcement zones in 12 areas, meaning homeless encampments will be allowed to flourish.
FOXLA reporter Matt Seedorff explained the 12-3 vote basically solidified the non-enforcement of the no camping code since some of the areas he checked out already had homeless encampments.
Residents and workers near the zones told Seedorff they already have concerns about safety, especially during the nighttime.
Councilman Hugo Soto Martinez, who pushed for the enforcement zones' removal and is a Democratic Socialist, told FOXLA that the bans on encampments make it "more difficult to engage with and support people experiencing homelessness."

One of the council members who voted against the proposal said her concern is that this is just the beginning, with more zones around Los Angeles being removed.
The second example comes from Mayor Karen Bass. The incumbent candidate posted a video bragging how for every dollar someone donates to her campaign, the city will match the donation 6-1. Meaning taxpayers, who are already being squeezed, are helping fund the mayor's candidacy.
Also known as the supermatch public financing program, it has been sold as a way to "reduce the influence of wealthy special interests in local elections."

It boggles the mind to see a city that desperately has called for bailouts for its budget, deciding to fund campaigns for itself through taxpayers. They can't fund the fire department adequately or fix the failing infrastructure, but hey, let's give the poor excuse of a mayor more money for her campaign.
While I appreciate conservatives who have decided to stick it out and fight for Los Angeles, and California, to return it to normalcy, I personally can't stand the thought of being taxed up to my eyeballs and for that money to go towards things other than basic services and a good quality of life.
Los Angeles had an opportunity to turn the ship around with candidate Spencer Pratt, but voters and the political machine decided they would rather burn it all down before letting that happen.

Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today: Time to reset the clock on Los Angeles finding new ways to get into the national spotlight over the backward decisions made by Democrat leaders. This week's first example is the city council approving, by a large majority, the removal of homeless enforcement zones in 12 areas, meaning homeless encampments will be allowed to flourish. FOXLA reporter Matt Seedorff explained the 12-3 vote basically solidified the non-enforcement of the no camping code since some of the areas he checked out already had homeless encampments. Residents and workers near the zones told Seedorff they already have concerns about safety, especially during the nighttime. Councilman Hugo Soto Martinez, who pushed for the enforcement zones' removal and is a Democratic Socialist, told FOXLA that the bans on encampments make it "more difficult to engage with and support people experiencing homelessness." One of the council members who voted against the proposal said her concern is that this is just the beginning, with more zones around Los Angeles being removed. The second example comes from Mayor Karen Bass. The incumbent candidate posted a video bragging how for every dollar someone donates to her campaign, the city will match the donation 6-1. Meaning taxpayers, who are already being squeezed, are helping fund the mayor's candidacy. Also known as the supermatch public financing program, it has been sold as a way to "reduce the influence of wealthy special interests in local elections." While I appreciate conservatives who have decided to stick it out and fight for Los Angeles, and California, to return it to normalcy, I personally can't stand the thought of being taxed up to my eyeballs and for that money to go towards things other than basic services and a good quality of life. Peter,
**If you’ve turned on the TV recently, you know the Republican midterm media blitz is officially in full swing here in North Carolina.**
That’s why we’re rolling out a new survey to a select number of supporters to gauge how your news intake is impacting your view on our campaign, this Senate race and Roy Cooper himself. It’s clear that Republicans are terrified of our grassroots momentum. Since launching a new multimillion-dollar attack ad campaign across broadcast, cable and streaming, the Senate GOP’s top super PAC is officially spending more here than in any other battleground race.
With polls tightening, we worry their negative media investments are paying off – but as we enter the final leg of the race that will decide Senate control, we can’t leave anything up to chance.

* * *
I was back on NewsNation Thursday night, debating immigration on Katie Pavlich's show. Sitting across from me was Tricia McLaughlin, former DHS spokesperson and one of the most prolific liars to ever grace the American government. Which, if you've been paying attention, is really saying something.
And Tricia did what Tricia always does. She lied her ass off about immigrants in this country.
I've debated a lot of professional liars over the last year. I've come to expect it. But something about sitting next to Tricia McLaughlin on Thursday set me off, because I simply could not put up with her bullshit for one more second.
So I called her a liar to her face. And I reminded the American people exactly who and what she is.
She called it "character assassination." Maybe I'd feel bad about that if I thought she had a character to assassinate.
So let me remind you who Tricia McLaughlin is.
She's a woman who stole $220 million in taxpayer money by secretly funneling it to her own husband's firm. That alone should have ended her career. Instead, she gets to go on TV and feel important/
And as a taxpayer-funded spokesperson, here's a partial list of what she lied about:
* **A Chicago mom shot five times by Border Patrol.** Tricia said the woman rammed agents. The body cam shows the agent swerved into her. The government admitted it in court. Her tweet is still up.

* **Renee Good and Alex Pretti, killed by federal agents in Minneapolis.** Tricia called them domestic terrorists who wanted to massacre law enforcement. Video showed Pretti never drew his gun. It was dissent. Even this administration backed off. She didn't.

* **A grieving mother who miscarried in ICE custody.** Tricia smeared her as a wanted criminal. Court documents prove the warrant had been thrown out. She never corrected it.

* **A teenage girl violently detained on camera.** Tricia claimed it was year-old footage of Chicago PD arresting a burglar. It wasn't.

* **A TV news producer.** Tricia said she threw objects at Border Patrol. Bystander video contradicted her. The woman was never charged with anything.

* **And her signature line, that ICE targets "the worst of the worst."** ICE's own numbers: 73% of people booked since October had no criminal conviction.

This is a person who lies the way the rest of us breathe.
The reason she worked for Donald Trump is because she lies the way he does and she steals the way he does. That's the whole job description. He surrounds himself with people who have already decided that proximity to power and money is worth whatever's left of their soul. Tricia made that trade a long time ago. Now she gets to go on TV and keep lying, keep grifting, keep doing the thing she was hired to do, except now she's doing it on a cable network instead of from you.

* * *
I tweeted the video out. Katie Pavlich was not happy about that. She responded that Tricia is welcome on her show anytime to talk about "violent illegal aliens," and that she wants guests who will call out anyone who commits heinous crimes like murder, rape, or trafficking.
For a second I thought she was talking about the Trump administration. Or the Epstein files. Or the Tate brothers.
But no. She was talking about immigrants who were living here peacefully.
Look, I'm in favor of removing anyone who commits a violent act. Of course I am. Who isn't? I'm in favor of securing the border. I think Democrats have, at times, not been strong enough on it, and I've said so. But the immigration policies of this administration are indefensible. That's precisely why people like Tricia McLaughlin have to lie about them all the goddamn time. You don't need to fabricate a story about a mother who miscarried in custody if the truth is on your side.
There is no reason for her to be on television. It is irresponsible to hand a microphone to someone who lies this brazenly. But they're going to keep booking her, because she'll sell whatever racist slop they come up with to scare people. That is the service she provides. And we should all be outraged by it.
And that's the thing. This comes back to the thing at the core of this newsletter, the thing I keep coming back to with all of you: there is no accountability for anything that happens in Washington.
There is zero gravity in DC. You can say whatever you want. Do whatever you want. Steal whatever you want. Hurt whoever you want. Nothing ever lands. Nobody ever falls.
In fact, the only accountability coming out of Thursday night is that I probably won't be invited back on Katie's show. And that's fine. I've got plenty of shit to do. I appreciate the opportunity, and I love a lot of people at NewsNation. But that segment was ridiculous, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
If we're going to live in a civil society, if we're going to save this democracy, if we're ever going to get back to a place where we don't hate each other, then not handing airtime to people who stole from the American taxpayer and lied to the American people on the taxpayer's dime is probably a good fucking start.
People need to be held accountable for the lies they tell. For the lives they ruin. For the crimes they commit. I don't think that's a radical idea. I think it's supposed to be the basis of this entire country. Instead we've become a goddamn banana republic, and it's disgusting.
None of this is new. And it's hard to stay this angry all the time when there's so much to be angry about.

This system needs to be fixed. It needs to be torn down and rebuilt. And it's going to take a lot of us saying enough is enough to get there.
I'm saying it. I hope you'll say it with me.
With urgency,
--Mike

| | Peter, I ran for office because I persistently witnessed my patients facing impossible choices: **Do I pay for the healthcare I need, or do I pay my rent? Do I buy my prescriptions, or do I put food on the table?** These are not choices any hardworking person should have to make. I’m sounding the alarm because **we are already in a healthcare crisis.** We cannot wait until it gets worse to act. Donald Trump has spent years undermining the public health systems that keep our communities safe and healthy. His Medicaid cuts put community health centers and rural hospitals at much greater risk, threatening access to care for millions of Americans and putting even more strain on an already stretched healthcare workforce. Now, he has launched yet another attack on vaccines, disregarding decades of scientific evidence and the guidance of public health experts. **I know what happens when people cannot afford care. ** We have a chance to change course this November and bring back some stability, protections, experts, and sanity to the House. That’s why I’m honored to be endorsed by healthcare organizations I deeply admire, including Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Care for U.S., and Oregon Nurses Association.

### From Lincoln to Mao: How the 2026 DSA Platform Breaks from the American Political Tradition

When the Democratic Socialists of America released its 2026 platform, "[Workers Deserve More](https://substack.com/redirect/3ea316c8-b4bc-4dd8-9152-da2e225fc042?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," it presented a vision of governance that would have been unrecognizable to Abraham Lincoln--and antithetical to the Republican Party he helped build. While Lincoln and the antebellum Republicans argued for constitutional liberty and free labor within America's existing framework, and while Reagan-era Republicans championed limited government and individual freedom, the DSA's 2026 program calls for the abolition of police, prisons, the Senate, the Supreme Court, the Electoral College, and national borders, alongside the nationalization of private corporations and state-run healthcare. A close comparison reveals that the DSA platform bears a far stronger resemblance to Mao Zedong's ideology of perpetual class struggle and institutional demolition than to either Lincoln's Republicanism or the conservatism of the Reagan era.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ae6e337e-eb88-40a5-8ff4-2cb9100f958c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Lincoln and the Republican Founding: Rule of Law and Free Labor**
The Lincoln-Douglas debates of 1858 centered on the expansion of slavery, but Lincoln's arguments were deeply rooted in constitutional process and moral persuasion. He opposed the extension of slavery into new territories and warned that a "house divided" could not stand, yet he never called for abolishing existing constitutional structures. The Republican Party was founded on the slogan "Free Soil, Free Labor, Free Men," emphasizing individual opportunity and government protection of rights rather than government ownership of industry. Lincoln's 1860 platform opposed slavery's expansion but accepted constitutional limits on ending slavery where it already existed. The party's core philosophy was incremental, legal, and institutional: it sought to end a great moral evil through speeches, elections, and legislation--not by dismantling the Senate, courts, or borders.
This tradition continued into the Reagan era. The 1980 Republican platform emphasized "lower taxes, limited government," free enterprise, and individual liberty. Reagan conservatism was suspicious of state power, championed free markets, and framed American government as one of enumerated powers--a direct inheritance of the founders' skepticism of centralized authority. Whether one agrees with its specifics, the Reagan Republican tradition saw the individual, not the collective, as the locus of sovereignty.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8c37767d-a6e8-48b0-aea3-a6ae91dd049e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The DSA 's 2026 Platform: Institutional Abolition and State Control**
By contrast, the DSA's "Workers Deserve More" program reads as a blueprint for revolutionary transformation rather than reform. The platform explicitly demands abolishing the carceral state--police and prisons--while eliminating ICE and national borders. It calls for nationalizing private corporations, implementing state-run healthcare, imposing rent control, and providing free public college. Structurally, it seeks to abolish the Senate, replace the Supreme Court, eliminate the Electoral College, and extend voting rights to noncitizens. These are not policy tweaks; they are the wholesale demolition of America's constitutional architecture.
Where Lincoln cautiously respected constitutional boundaries even while challenging slavery, the DSA treats existing American institutions as illegitimate obstacles to be torn down. Where Reagan Republicans believed "peace through strength" and constitutional order preserved freedom, the DSA characterizes America's entire governmental framework as an apparatus of capitalism requiring destruction.
**Parallels to Mao: Perpetual Revolution and Class Enemies**
The DSA platform's language and logic map far more neatly onto Mao Zedong's ideology than onto Lincoln's republicanism. Mao's "Cultural Revolution" was built on the concept of perpetual class struggle--the idea that even after socialists seized power, reactionary elements remained embedded within society and its institutions, requiring constant purification through mass mobilization. Mao called for the destruction of the "Four Olds": old customs, old culture, old habits, and old ideas. This translated into purging universities, attacking the judiciary, demonizing "capitalist roaders," and dismantling traditional governance under the banner of revolutionary equality.
The DSA's calls to abolish police, prisons, courts, and the Senate function as an American analogue. Rather than reforming institutions, the platform demands their elimination, substituting mass democracy and worker control for constitutional checks and balances. Like Mao's Red Guards, DSA rhetoric frames political opposition not as disagreement but as structural evil--"capitalist," "carceral," or "fascist"--that must be uprooted. Mao sought to replace "bourgeois" authority with "people's" communes; the DSA explicitly aims to shift "structural political and economic power away from corporations and into the hands of the working class." Both treat private enterprise as an enemy class to be eliminated by state power.
Lincoln believed in a union of states with constitutional protections for individual rights; the DSA envisions a union of workers where nationalization replaces private property. Reagan Republicans warned that government expansion endangered liberty; the DSA proposes expanding state control over housing, healthcare, education, and industry to an extent Mao would recognize.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4e8b6c6a-730f-4032-92be-552aae89b99a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Why It Is Not Lincolnian**
The differences are philosophical, not merely partisan. Lincoln's Republicans saw government as a necessary protector of individual rights in a pluralistic society. They held debates, ran candidates, and passed laws. The DSA's 2026 program treats democratic capitalism itself as illegitimate and frames its mission as revolutionary transformation. Lincoln opposed slavery because it denied human beings the fruits of their own labor; the DSA opposes capitalism because it allows individuals to keep the fruits of their own labor. For Lincoln, freedom *from* state-compelled labor was the goal; for the DSA, freedom *through* state-compelled redistribution is the method.
Abraham Lincoln once said that America was the "last best hope of earth" because it offered self-government under law. The Reagan-era Republican platform affirmed that vision through limited government and economic freedom. The 2026 DSA platform, by contrast, borrows its structure not from Springfield, Illinois, or from the Constitution, but from the ideology of Mao's China: perpetual class struggle, the denunciation of existing institutions, and the conviction that only revolutionary demolition of the old order can birth a new society. In that sense, the platform is more Mao than Lincoln--and more revolution than republic.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b12e4d11-4ec7-41c4-ac6e-5a39f237544f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As the DSA's 2026 platform pushes beyond traditional left-wing reform into outright structural demolition--demanding the abolition of the Senate, Supreme Court, prisons, police, and national borders, while calling for the nationalization of private industry--the fault line between institutional Democrats and revolutionary democratic socialists is widening into a chasm that the party's "big tent" may no longer be able to contain. Where mainstream Democrats still operate within the framework of constitutional governance, seeking to expand the welfare state through legislation and elections, the DSA treats that same framework as an illegitimate bulwark of capitalism to be dismantled by mass mobilization. This is not merely a disagreement over the size of government or the pace of change; it is a collision between reform and revolution, between a party that wants to capture the state and a movement that wants to abolish its core institutions. Should the DSA continue to elect candidates who openly embrace platform positions that read like a Maoist wish list--while simultaneously threatening to primary establishment Democrats deemed insufficiently radical--the coming Civil War 2.0 may not be between left and right, but between Democrats and democratic socialists, turning what was once an internal coalition dispute into a genuine struggle for the identity, and possibly even the survival, of the oldest political party on Earth and the American center-left in a way that could reshape the two-party system or spark something far more dangerous than a primary challenge.

The DSA's 2026 program treats democratic capitalism itself as illegitimate and frames its mission as revolutionary transformation. Lincoln opposed slavery because it denied human beings the fruits of their own labor; the DSA opposes capitalism because it allows individuals to keep the fruits of their own labor. For Lincoln, freedom from state-compelled labor was the goal; for the DSA, freedom through state-compelled redistribution is the method. Abraham Lincoln once said that America was the "last best hope of earth" because it offered self-government under law. The Reagan-era Republican platform affirmed that vision through limited government and economic freedom. The 2026 DSA platform, by contrast, borrows its structure not from Springfield, Illinois, or from the Constitution, but from the ideology of Mao's China: perpetual class struggle, the denunciation of existing institutions, and the conviction that only revolutionary demolition of the old order can birth a new society. In that sense, the platform is more Mao than Lincoln--and more revolution than republic. | | ---|---|--- As the DSA's 2026 platform pushes beyond traditional left-wing reform into outright structural demolition--demanding the abolition of the Senate, Supreme Court, prisons, police, and national borders, while calling for the nationalization of private industry--the fault line between institutional Democrats and revolutionary democratic socialists is widening into a chasm that the party's "big tent" may no longer be able to contain. Where mainstream Democrats still operate within the framework of constitutional governance, seeking to expand the welfare state through legislation and elections, the DSA treats that same framework as an illegitimate bulwark of capitalism to be dismantled by mass mobilization. This is not merely a disagreement over the size of government or the pace of change; it is a collision between reform and revolution, between a party that wants to capture the state and a movement that wants to abolish its core institutions. Should the DSA continue to elect candidates who openly embrace platform positions that read like a Maoist wish list--while simultaneously threatening to primary establishment Democrats deemed insufficiently radical--the coming Civil War 2.0 may not be between left and right, but between Democrats and democratic socialists, turning what was once an internal coalition dispute into a genuine struggle for the identity, and possibly even the survival, of the oldest political party on Earth and the American center-left in a way that could reshape the two-party system or spark something far more dangerous than a primary challenge. | | ---|---|--- You're currently a free subscriber to . [ ]Tweet from @atruper: "WELKER: As Democratic leader in the House, would you vote for or against Medicare for All? In the same week, Yale published a new study showing MFA could save $1 TRILLION and 11,000 lives per year. And Data for Progress reports that 65 percent of ALL Americans across political parties support an MFA-style system; among Democrats, that support increases to 78 percent. Jeffries himself was previously a cosponsor from 2014 to 2021, so why is he changing his position when polls show more Americans support it now than ever before? Because as long as our Party is in the pockets of corporate PACs and lobbyists, it will always put their profits above the bold changes their constituents demand and deserve. clean_body: The fight continues. | | | We don’t know the ending to this story yet. But thanks to activists like you, we were able to win the first round. Let’s set the scene for a second: Earlier this year, Georgia Republicans decided to try to take advantage of a new Supreme Court ruling gutting the Voting Rights Act. They wanted to draw new voting maps that would rip political power away from Black and brown voters and give the GOP a huge structural advantage. But we were able to fight back right away — thanks to a strong foundation built by this community. Georgians got organized, filled buses, and packed the state capitol to say “hands off our votes!” in numbers that could not be ignored. Republican legislators got scared of the backlash. They gave up on rigging maps — for now. But they’re ready to try again as soon as they think we’re not paying attention. That’s why we’ve been connecting Georgians to information about their State Representatives — so they can get ready to hold them accountable at the ballot box. State House Republicans have shown their true colors, and we’ve got a real chance to flip the House this November to defend democracy going forward. Even when one chapter ends, the bigger fight continues. That’s why we count on ongoing support from dedicated donors to fuel this year-round work. And that’s why we’re grateful to have vigilant activists like you on the team. Thank you for everything you do to defend the freedom to vote and ensure a truly representative democracy. Friend, Since Donald Trump returned to office, his administration has deployed ICE terror to our cities and communities across the country ― kidnapping our neighbors and family members, torturing detainees in ICE detention centers, and even killing people in our streets. **Now, we’ve learned of two major escalations in ICE harassment and violence.** In a dramatic violation of privacy rights, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is sharing airline passenger names, birthdates, and other information with ICE. According to a _Freedom of Information Act_ lawsuit, this agreement has been in place since May of 2025 and runs contrary to the sworn congressional testimony from the Trump administration’s acting TSA Administrator from earlier this year.1 **This TSA/ICE data sharing has led to a surge in arrests at airports with ICE even targeting immigrants who have employment authorization, who are recently married to a U.S. citizen, and who are awaiting visa extensions.** One ICE source called kidnapping immigrants at airports “easy targets.”2 At the same time, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is reportedly in the process of procuring electric shock gloves to subdue people as part of its mass deportation agenda. We should be abolishing ICE, not providing them with more weapons to harm our communities. I have introduced the _No TSA Data for ICE Act_ to immediately halt coordination between TSA and ICE. But Congress must go much further to protect our residents from ICE violence and terror. [**Add your name as a grassroots co-sponsor of my _No TSA Data for ICE Act_ , and to demand Congress abolish ICE and ban any law enforcement entity from using electric shock gloves on our residents.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uDKkapQVnT18L0ER7M9FmlLV_cPuRDQ0ZUWhlG9VzS0vX5HQblrRyGqH8B-pisgLYHAphdufB9uAKODpW2YcOt1V1cBh1INnlRAh7bLAwk5qO7-wt6txfjwj5yceaesNajlgKDnmf5IZOiZJVlaOR75yJbwVd4tOynFiFztgQrlUXz5g5jshCi6wM5uyf8RITxzlT9EqC6-UunsrcRb9RppwqHt3DU9ycS5GIrz1hrfluxtwTsNaAIVT1OLkF05SCHskGOxgIV494xeUe_f20S7BhjnqLO7TFwmbXXgLT1SX8duE89TqOl0xevAu-RUxJcOHLxzMcJ5tvrsDHWlJ2T8EK9ecfeNQCWGM7QCclDLl4wt7G95EFnHqdqLur2ANs0uwVcgQHl7e-Bxc5gEnc8xQR0B-PF0Yiu1KnmxzmRJiX9lulHsBTZynPNf3oA-cuzs0AQTIDL-B9IkzqXPmoToKSc71QxXWkMeqK-XirPg/4te/Tf3FAUcwSXmhuv-Ca_ccig/h1/h001.4hPY_LxI47kueiB-Inka27HWIANgAB79ENuvK6x1deQ) | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uDKkapQVnT18L0ER7M9FmlLV_cPuRDQ0ZUWhlG9VzS0vX5HQblrRyGqH8B-pisgLYHAphdufB9uAKODpW2YcOt1V1cBh1INnlRAh7bLAwk5qO7-wt6txfjwj5yceaesNWRyLgpWTkV9wBld0pIfrXDn36Ewm3T1IlmdimWVQqHboBFoHw92mvqO-XZEAzCufTOf9ePfstM7PNRyhA0d2jXMGiNyQNWwIKKRntqYpNgr0QwncXYArtoaVJcouKSm9hBOcQisjtlUmakBEubX_eP3_4CmPhw3yzmRUYCz7mBXRr_wjIW_dr6tv7FNg_WYGFILcL5X9euubfDAA0TmMH5GIBiZDLjkm8EHKfWLpZpICVJuQT1VqYBpOWjQRmYfoSu6WRsAio4kZBc-Cx4gFc-S5BJC-EDUva2uAIIKVL71jHcHtsSNq5vuDnDqXIWx2MARHN-bNJJbqJj8nSE33bFNqkhg3zijfreSusENKJHg/4te/Tf3FAUcwSXmhuv-Ca_ccig/h2/h001._fQKPQg1qWNTmaaP4_xl1bCKiJmmQfmDLDHiKfkiyxk)

TSA and ICE have only been in existence since 2001 and 2002. Congress created these agencies and can abolish them. But even many of my Democratic colleagues have been resistant to abolishing ICE, which is why we need to grow our movement, not just to hold ICE accountable, but to end their terror immediately.

| Letter from the Chair
---
Fellow Republicans,
This week, my friend Rob Rohrbough, who is a thoughtful, faith-filled, and reasoned thinker shared with me some of his thoughts on the necessity of the Christian vote. I want to pass on his thoughts to you. The Bill of Rights to the US Constitution includes in the First Amendment "Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof." This right is important to people of all faiths. We have seen in Communist countries where faith in God is suppressed, attacked, and/or abolished by government in order to have government replace God as the arbiter of our conscience and conduct. We have history to show us and our faith to guide us, so let us not sleepwalk into allowing it to happen in the Nebraska or the United States at large.
Pews to Politics Why Christians Need to be Involved in Politics Saturday, August 8, 2026 Rob Rohrbough

Have you ever thought politics was dirty and messy? As Christians, the most important thing in our lives is our relationship with Jesus Christ. Does it stop there? What about the Great Commission? What about defending our right to carry out The Great Commission? Or even practice Christianity?
Do you know that there is a movement to take away your right to evangelize? In 1964 the Department of Education implemented the results mainly of three court cases -- McCollum v Board of Education in 1948, Engel v Vitale in 1962, and Murray v Curlett in 1963 -- to remove God, prayer, and the Bible from public schools. How can we expect the Christian culture upon which our nation was founded to continue? That precedent has encouraged movement to a more secular society over the past 60+ years. Church attendance has dropped and more people consider capitalism to be evil and selfish. Young people in particular are starting to consider socialism a preferable economic model.
With that background, how can church-going Christians be content to let others determine how government should work? Who gets elected? There is an old cliche -- if Christians do not get involved in politics, they will be ruled by those who do not believe nor share their values. Our current president put it even more strongly -- "If Christians don't get involved in politics, politics will erase their right to be Christians." These are no idle speculations. I have observed the willful decline over six decades.
So, what do we do? Register to vote if you haven't already. Don't register as an independent. Register in a party so you can have influence in it. Be sure your party supports Christian principles and values. Become active in it. Examine its platform so you know where it stands. Long term, influence the platform if it does not fully support those values. Once you are comfortable with your party's principles, examine the candidates and how they align with those principles and your priorities as a Christian. Help them win in every way you can with your time, talent, and treasure.

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair Fellow Republicans, This week, my friend Rob Rohrbough, who is a thoughtful, faith-filled, and reasoned thinker shared with me some of his thoughts on the necessity of the Christian vote. I want to pass on his thoughts to you. The Bill of Rights to the US Constitution includes in the First Amendment "Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof." This right is important to people of all faiths. We have seen in Communist countries where faith in God is suppressed, attacked, and/or abolished by government in order to have government replace God as the arbiter of our conscience and conduct. We have history to show us and our faith to guide us, so let us not sleepwalk into allowing it to happen in the Nebraska or the United States at large. Pews to Politics Why Christians Need to be Involved in Politics Saturday, August 8, 2026 Rob Rohrbough Have you ever thought politics was dirty and messy? As Christians, the most important thing in our lives is our relationship with Jesus Christ. Does it stop there? What about the Great Commission? What about defending our right to carry out The Great Commission? Or even practice Christianity? Do you know that there is a movement to take away your right to evangelize? In 1964 the Department of Education implemented the results mainly of three court cases -- McCollum v Board of Education in 1948, Engel v Vitale in 1962, and Murray v Curlett in 1963 -- to remove God, prayer, and the Bible from public schools. How can we expect the Christian culture upon which our nation was founded to continue? That precedent has encouraged movement to a more secular society over the past 60+ years. Church attendance has dropped and more people consider capitalism to be evil and selfish. Young people in particular are starting to consider socialism a preferable economic model. With that background, how can church-going Christians be content to let others determine how government should work? Who gets elected? There is an old cliche -- if Christians do not get involved in politics, they will be ruled by those who do not believe nor share their values. Our current president put it even more strongly -- "If Christians don't get involved in politics, politics will erase their right to be Christians." These are no idle speculations. I have observed the willful decline over six decades. So, what do we do? Register to vote if you haven't already. Don't register as an independent. Register in a party so you can have influence in it. Be sure your party supports Christian principles and values. Become active in it. Examine its platform so you know where it stands. Long term, influence the platform if it does not fully support those values. Once you are comfortable with your party's principles, examine the candidates and how they align with those principles and your priorities as a Christian. Help them win in every way you can with your time, talent, and treasure. Short term, identify others who sit with you on that pew and are not active politically. Help them understand how important it is to get involved. You have several resources at your command to prepare you for the task. Here are a few from my Facebook page: Christians not to fall into Satan's trap == and the need to return to Jesus Christ. to engage David and Tim Barton's answer to, "==" And a few more: The sin of pietism -- == Kirk's minister). on 250th) == (also Wallbuilders) Those who disagree with you know how to get out the vote, and they do not intend to allow Christianity to thrive. Lord of Hosts Church encourages their members to be active politically. Dr. Dodd at Westside Church does a good job. Some churches, including mine, do not encourage political activity. Does yours? Would the United States exist without the activism of preachers like the Muellenberg brothers? Would Christianity be one of the three major world religions had the Apostles Paul or Luke worried only about their own relationship with Christ? When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn. Proverbs 29:2 (KJV) | | == | Together, We Win! name: Swing Left
subject: A Democratic governor in Ohio breaks the GOP trifecta
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
A competitive Senate race could benefit Democrats across the state.
#
Hi there,
Ohio holds some of the highest-leverage opportunities on our map, and is a critical state for building Democratic groundwork for wins in 2026 and beyond.
The governor’s race is one of Swing Left’s “Reach Races” this year, which means winning here will be more of a stretch—but possible considering the current political climate leaning towards Democrats and recent polling showing the candidates separated by just 1 or 2 points.
Democrats have an exceptionally strong gubernatorial candidate in **Dr. Amy Acton.** And with former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown expected to drive massive turnout in his race to reclaim a Senate seat, the governor's race is poised to benefit directly from Ohio's biggest Democratic mobilization effort in years. Dr. Acton faces**Republican nominee Vivek Ramaswamy** , who has secured endorsements from both Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance.
Right now, Ohio Republicans hold the governor’s seat and both state legislatures—a full trifecta—and have used it aggressively to hold on to their power through redistricting and election law changes. Flipping the governor's mansion would break that trifecta and give Democrats a vital veto in the state.
**But winning the governor’s mansion is only part of the equation.**
Ohio Republicans currently hold a 65-seat supermajority in the State House. By flipping six seats in the State House, or five seats in the State Senate, Democrats can break the GOP’s 60-vote supermajority.
That matters because a Democratic governor can only use their veto power effectively if Republicans don’t have enough votes to override it. It would also stop Republicans from being able to place constitutional resolutions on the ballot without bipartisan support.
State legislatures decide voting laws, how district maps are drawn, and which rights are protected. Building Democratic power in Ohio isn't optional; it's essential to laying the groundwork for 2026, 2028, and beyond. That’s why Swing Left is investing in both the governor’s race and the state legislative races. Together, they can fundamentally change the balance of power in Ohio.
**[Will you make a donation of any amount to the Ohio Win in the States Fund today to help break the Republican supermajority in the State House, gain seats in the State Senate, and help elect Amy Acton as the next Governor of Ohio?](https://act.swingleft.org/go/66?c0=sl-states-oh-2026.7usj9U&refcode=em20260822-2535&t=1&akid=2535%2E1562180%2E08rQpx)**
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/66?c0=sl-states-oh-2026.7usj9U&refcode=em20260822-2535&t=2&akid=2535%2E1562180%2E08rQpx)**
Thank you for being part of this work.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. ### Dams Are Lifelines: Why Removing the Potter Valley River Dams Would Cripple the West
| | [Heartland Journal ®](https://substack.com/@heartlandjournal)
---
| Aug 22
---
| [](https://substack.com/@heartlandjournal)

---

---

Across the American West, water is not a convenience--it is the foundation of survival. From the orchards of Northern California to the wheat fields of Washington State, a silent crisis is unfolding as activists and regulators push to remove critical dams that store and deliver the region's most precious resource. The proposed decommissioning of the Potter Valley Project in California and the Snake River dams in Washington is not merely an environmental debate. It is an existential threat to farmers, firefighters, and the rural communities that depend on reliable water. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission must see these proposals for what they are--a reckless gamble with American food security and public safety--and halt any action that would remove these structures.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d1155146-f346-4510-888b-e5333e8b6833?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Potter Valley Project, operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Company, is a remarkable feat of engineering that diverts water from the upper Eel River basin into the East Branch Russian River serving 750,000 residents. For more than a century, this flow has sustained hundreds of farms, vineyards, dairies, and ranches in Mendocino and Sonoma counties. It feeds the town of Potter Valley directly and underpins the agricultural economy that makes the region productive. Without the diversion, the Russian River basin loses a vital source of supply during the dry summer months, precisely when crops need irrigation and communities face drought stress.
California does not have a water problem; it has a water storage problem. Removing the Potter Valley dams would eliminate that storage and diversion capacity, turning a managed resource into an unreliable trickle. Farmers who have invested generations in their land would be forced to fallow fields, sell livestock, or abandon operations entirely. The surrounding towns, already stretched thin, would see their tax bases evaporate. In a state that produces two-thirds of the nation's fruits and nuts, choking off Northern California irrigation is not a local issue--it is a national food security crisis.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1e970f04-7874-4537-9762-11cc2c32c6a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then there is the matter of fire. Californians do not need a reminder that wildfire season is no longer a season; it is a year-round reality. When walls of flame descend on rural communities, every gallon of accessible water matters. The reservoirs created by the Potter Valley Project provide critical dip sites for aerial firefighting crews and drafting locations for rural fire departments that often lack municipal hydrant systems. Decommissioning these dams and draining their reservoirs would remove emergency water sources from some of the most fire-prone terrain in the country. Fire services already operate on shoestring budgets in Mendocino County; forcing them to haul water over greater distances while a fire rages is not policy--it is negligence.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.agszhCcCMKBBgEqJg0UEmN5BwERo4_Pc-FzehhIFrVA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=211458068)
Northward in Washington State, the lower Snake River dams--Ice Harbor, Lower Monumental, Little Goose, and Lower Granite--form another linchpin of regional survival. While much of the public debate centers on hydropower and barge traffic, the water management role of these structures is equally vital. They regulate flows that support extensive irrigation networks across southeastern Washington, feeding a agricultural sector that produces wheat, potatoes, onions, and legumes for global markets. The reservoirs provide the stable water elevations that allow irrigation pumps to function and that recharge aquifers used by rural municipalities.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/55335cd8-9470-423f-9a8b-dfc318eaed32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Removing the Snake River dams would not magically restore an uninterrupted river. It would sever the water delivery mechanism that farmers and ranchers have relied upon for decades. Eastern Washington is dry country. It lacks the consistent rainfall of the Cascades' western slope. Without managed storage and regulated flows, farmland reverts to dust. The small communities that line the Snake and its tributaries--from the Tri-Cities to Lewiston--depend on this system for household water, agricultural processing, and local industry. Dam removal would not just inconvenience these towns; it would gut them.
Like their counterparts in California, Washington fire services depend on accessible water in rural landscapes. The Snake River reservoirs serve as strategic reserves for wildfire suppression across the Palouse and Columbia Plateau, where summer lightning storms and tinder-dry grasses create relentless fire risk. Aerial crews and ground teams use these water bodies as immediate sources to protect homes, ranches, and critical infrastructure. Decommissioning the dams in the name of ecological theory while ignoring the life-or-death logistics of firefighting is a trade that Washington residents should refuse to accept.
The broader economic ripples extend far beyond the farm gate. When a region loses irrigation, it does not only lose crops; it loses trucking companies, equipment dealers, meat processors, wineries, and the Main Street businesses that serve them. Schools close. Hospitals shrink. Young families leave because there is no economic future. Decommissioning these dams would be an exercise in rural erasure, wiping towns off the map because distant policymakers decided that fish recovery requires destroying human communities--despite technological alternatives like advanced fish passage systems, hatchery reform, and habitat restoration that do not require dam removal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa7b8500-bd91-4c49-a57e-4f44f4eccec2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is where FERC must step in. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission is charged with balancing environmental stewardship with the public interest, and that interest explicitly includes reliable water supply, power generation, and economic stability. Under federal law, any proposal to decommission a licensed hydroelectric project must undergo rigorous scrutiny of not only ecological but also socioeconomic impacts. FERC cannot allow itself to become a rubber stamp for removal campaigns that treat agriculture and public safety as acceptable collateral damage.
The commission must recognize that the National Environmental Policy Act and the Federal Power Act require a holistic review. An environmental impact statement that ignores evaporating farms, abandoned firefighting assets, and dying rural economies is not science; it is advocacy masquerading as regulation. If PG&E seeks to shed its Potter Valley license, FERC must ensure that any successor operator maintains the project intact. If federal agencies advance Snake River dam removal, FERC should use its authority and public platform to oppose the destruction of essential water infrastructure. There are better ways to help salmon than by damning farmers and firefighters to failure.
America's Western dams were built by generations who understood that prosperity in an arid landscape requires foresight. They captured spring snowmelt and stored it for summer crops, autumn fires, and year-round human need. The proposal to tear down the Potter Valley and Snake River dams ignores that wisdom. Farmers deserve to keep their water. Firefighters deserve to keep their reservoirs. Rural families deserve to keep their homes. FERC has the power to protect them all. It must act--and it must say no to decommissioning.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/896b3c9b-20ae-4e6f-a073-b672ebcf870e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A final note of caution to the Commissioners: The Supreme Court's landmark decision in Trump v. Slaughter has obliterated the "for cause" removal protections that once insulated independent agencies like FERC from raw partisan discharge, meaning President Trump can now fire any commissioner without cause, explanation, or due process--policy disagreement alone is sufficient to end your tenure overnight. If you approve decommissioning orders that sever water supplies to farms, drain critical firefighting reservoirs, and devastate the rural communities you are sworn to serve, you will face not only the wrath of Western landowners and emergency services, but the certainty that your seats are politically expendable in a single afternoon. Your predecessors believed their independence was constitutionally bulletproof; the Court has proven otherwise. Unless you wish to be replaced by commissioners who understand that these dams are the difference between agricultural survival and rural collapse, you would be wise to reject these removal applications immediately and protect the water infrastructure that keeps the West alive.

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission is charged with balancing environmental stewardship with the public interest, and that interest explicitly includes reliable water supply, power generation, and economic stability. Under federal law, any proposal to decommission a licensed hydroelectric project must undergo rigorous scrutiny of not only ecological but also socioeconomic impacts. FERC cannot allow itself to become a rubber stamp for removal campaigns that treat agriculture and public safety as acceptable collateral damage. The commission must recognize that the National Environmental Policy Act and the Federal Power Act require a holistic review. An environmental impact statement that ignores evaporating farms, abandoned firefighting assets, and dying rural economies is not science; it is advocacy masquerading as regulation. If PG&E seeks to shed its Potter Valley license, FERC must ensure that any successor operator maintains the project intact. If federal agencies advance Snake River dam removal, FERC should use its authority and public platform to oppose the destruction of essential water infrastructure. There are better ways to help salmon than by damning farmers and firefighters to failure. America's Western dams were built by generations who understood that prosperity in an arid landscape requires foresight. They captured spring snowmelt and stored it for summer crops, autumn fires, and year-round human need. The proposal to tear down the Potter Valley and Snake River dams ignores that wisdom. Farmers deserve to keep their water. Firefighters deserve to keep their reservoirs. Rural families deserve to keep their homes. FERC has the power to protect them all. It must act--and it must say no to decommissioning. | | ---|---|--- A final note of caution to the Commissioners: The Supreme Court's landmark decision in Trump v. Slaughter has obliterated the "for cause" removal protections that once insulated independent agencies like FERC from raw partisan discharge, meaning President Trump can now fire any commissioner without cause, explanation, or due process--policy disagreement alone is sufficient to end your tenure overnight. If you approve decommissioning orders that sever water supplies to farms, drain critical firefighting reservoirs, and devastate the rural communities you are sworn to serve, you will face not only the wrath of Western landowners and emergency services, but the certainty that your seats are politically expendable in a single afternoon. Your predecessors believed their independence was constitutionally bulletproof; the Court has proven otherwise. Unless you wish to be replaced by commissioners who understand that these dams are the difference between agricultural survival and rural collapse, you would be wise to reject these removal applications immediately and protect the water infrastructure that keeps the West alive. A working democracy depends on a simple thing. The person who loses an election should be able to call the person who won and ask for a meeting. Not because they agree. Not because they like each other. Because the basic machinery of disagreement has to keep working after the votes are counted. When it stops working, something else takes its place.
What's taking its place right now, at every level of American politics, is a loyalty test. Surround yourself with people who flatter you. Treat criticism as betrayal. Punish dissent. Reward only the allies who never questioned you. We're watching this happen at the national level in real time. It's also happening quietly in states like mine.
I've been carrying this story for almost two years. I'm finally writing it down.
I've known John Curtis for a long time. Long before I ran against him, I worked with him as an environmental advocate. I sat in a small meeting with him for hours, alongside climbers from the American Alpine Club, talking about Bears Ears. He listened. He asked good questions. He was an advocate when it mattered. I enjoyed his sense of humor, his socks, his love for the outdoors. When he replaced Jason Chaffetz in Congress, it felt like an upgrade. I thought he was someone Utah could depend on.
That's the John Curtis I'm writing to.

I ran against him for U.S. Senate in 2024. Nearly half a million Utahns voted for me. I raised real concerns about the climate crisis, public lands, reproductive freedom, and the dangerous influence of Project 2025. I lost. He won, decisively. After the dust settled, I did what I thought was the basic thing a former opponent should do. I asked for a meeting.

In December 2024, I messaged his chief of staff, Corey Norman, before a trip to Washington. I was flexible: a hallway chat, a walk-and-talk, anything to show that we could move forward with respect, even after disagreement.
His response was, "We're full. Sorry." Then he sent screenshots of my social media posts. He told me my criticism was "bad behavior" and said he wouldn't "reward" it.
That same week, I saw John Curtis at the airport. I approached him calmly and said the campaign had been spirited, but I wanted to put the past behind us to work together on climate and public lands. He scolded me at baggage claim while waiting for his moving boxes. He asked if I really believed the things I said about him. He told me I had a credibility problem.
That was almost two years ago. It's stayed with me since.
I said hard things about his record during the campaign. I stand by them. I said he had lied. He had. I said he campaigned for Donald Trump in other states. He did. I said he put corporate interests ahead of the environment. His voting record proves it, and nineteen months in, his lifetime environmental voting record is worse than Mike Lee's. None of those critiques were personal attacks. They were about votes, about money, about the gap between what he said and what he did. I criticized the senator. I never went after the man.
The numbers back this up. The Heritage Foundation is the architect of Project 2025. Heritage Action, its lobbying arm, gives Curtis a 94% score for how he's voted this session and an 89% lifetime score. During Trump's first term, when Curtis was in the House, FiveThirtyEight found he voted with Trump's position 94% of the time. He can call himself a moderate. The numbers tell a different story.
I ran because I believed a strong opponent could push John Curtis to become the senator he was capable of being. A statesman in the tradition of Mitt Romney or John McCain. A senator who hadn't been radicalized. Who voted his conscience. Who put principles above party. Utah needs that kind of senator right now. As Trump dismantles environmental protections, guts the agencies that keep our air and water safe, and sells off public lands, we need someone who will actually push back. Not talk. Push. Nineteen months in, Curtis is doing the bare minimum. He can do more. He has done more, in the past, on issues that mattered.
A senator who feels secure in his mandate doesn't need to refuse meetings with the people who disagreed with him. A senator who trusts his own record doesn't need his chief of staff sending screenshots as a form of punishment. A senator who understands the office doesn't scold a former opponent at baggage claim. These aren't questions of personality. They're questions of what the office requires.
I want to be honest about why I waited this long to write it down.
I could have written this in December 2024. It happened. I had the receipts. Any editor would have run it. I didn't, because I kept hoping the story would resolve. That some meeting would happen. That he would grow into the office. That the pattern would break on its own. It didn't. He is not becoming Mitt Romney. He is becoming exactly what I said he would become during the campaign.
I also didn't write it because I was afraid. I still am, honestly. I know what it costs to disagree publicly. I've paid a version of that price for almost two years. Brand partnerships paused. Inbound opportunities slowed. Doors that used to open easily started sticking. Some of that is just how brands manage uncertainty. Some of it is the cost of running for office as a working content creator. But the threshold for what counts as "too controversial" is lower for women who challenge established male authority. That's not a theory. That's the bill I'm still paying.
What I've paid is nothing compared to what a senator risks when he breaks with his party or his president. But that's exactly the point. The office comes with more power and more protection than any of us have. If moral courage is possible anywhere, it's possible from a Senate seat. Utah didn't send John Curtis to Washington to do the safe thing. We sent him to do the right one, even when it costs him.

I know there's a cultural piece to this in Utah that goes unspoken. In a state where cultural power has long flowed through older men, particularly within the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, younger women who challenge that hierarchy get read as "out of line" before anyone considers what they actually said. A man my age raising the same questions about Curtis's record might be called ambitious. I got called difficult. Corey didn't engage with anything I said on the merits. He sent screenshots and a scolding. It doesn't have to define this relationship going forward.
What changed for me is what I'm watching at the national level from President Trump. There's the loyalty tests, the punishment of dissent and the treatment of criticism as betrayal. That's exactly what Curtis's office did to me on a smaller scale, and I'd been reading it as personal when it was actually structural. It's the same playbook. Small offices practice what large ones execute. If I don't name the small version, I have less standing to challenge the big one.
Senator Curtis will be in the Senate until January 2031. That's four and a half more years to decide what kind of senator he is going to be. Four and a half more years to decide whether he wants to be remembered as someone who grew into the office or someone who shrank inside it.
If I could go back and respond to Corey now, here's what I'd say:
_I appreciate your message, and I 've been thinking about this for the past nineteen months. During the campaign, I raised policy concerns that nearly half a million Utahns shared when they voted for me. That's not bad behavior. That's democracy. At a time when autocracy is on the rise, we need to show what respectful disagreement and reconciliation can look like. I'd still like to meet with you, or the Senator, or your staff. I'd even love to do a podcast or an Instagram Live to show how we can move forward and work together. That kind of leadership matters more than ever. Thanks for considering. I hope we can turn the page._
That offer still stands.
Here is what I'm asking. Take the meeting. Not with me, necessarily. With the allies you've been icing out. With the constituents who voted for a different direction and deserve to be heard by their senator. With the people who challenged you and who might, if you let them, sharpen your thinking rather than threaten it. Nearly half a million Utahns are waiting to see whether you represent them too, or only the people who flatter you.
The John Curtis I met years ago in that Bears Ears meeting would take the meeting. He would listen. He would ask good questions. He would remember that the office belongs to all of Utah.
I still believe that senator exists. I'm inviting him back.That offer still stands.
Here is what I'm asking. Take the meeting. Not with me, necessarily. With the allies you've been icing out. With the constituents who voted for a different direction and deserve to be heard by their senator. With the people who challenged you and who might, if you let them, sharpen your thinking rather than threaten it. Nearly half a million Utahns are waiting to see whether you represent them too, or only the people who flatter you.
The John Curtis I met years ago in that Bears Ears meeting would take the meeting. He would listen. He would ask good questions. He would remember that the office belongs to all of Utah.
I still believe that senator exists. I'm inviting him back.

Empty streets. Plywood on the windows. Caution tape on the swing sets. And his private diary says he had doubts the whole time.

Dear Patriot,

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzZ9AAwAAAAAAoChvBsmjbvk8ZPEzzro5O5-evGBFK8Nle-kFISYiQdVdvvSaVYaLNEmhpDmTXybMISwYtpNnhzDZqlE85LyGXrN4odcDtC9Dmq9DTmrzA

Do you remember when it was only fifteen days?

Fifteen days to slow the spread. That was the promise they made you, and you believed it, because a doctor on television told you that the science demanded it and you are a decent person who did not want to hurt anybody.

Do you remember what your street sounded like that spring? Nothing at all — no traffic, no children playing outside, no church bells on Sunday morning. Only sirens, running all day and into the night, and the sound of your own television counting the dead.

Do you remember the plywood going up over the storefronts downtown? The caution tape wrapped around the swing sets? The arrows taped to the floor of the grocery store, and the man who shouted at you for standing too close to him in the aisle?

Fifteen days eventually became two years. So let me ask you the question that nobody in Washington has ever bothered to ask you.

What did those two years take from you?

Not from the country. From you.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzZ9AAwAAAAAAoChvBsn6MPCcKNvesETPGMTkzqj676BQL4KLb3JmwL2gMoGChLpGkkDIRZyATP5hiSrKtY3SI6VEaoA9Ti0h0PcosXbfzTZkfO1vJxYHA
Help me get you the answer, under oath.

Maybe it was the business — thirty years of your life invested in it, and then a paper sign taped to the glass. The big chain store down the road stayed open and sold the very same goods, because yours was ruled "non-essential." Some of you never opened those doors again.

Maybe it was your father's funeral, with only ten mourners permitted, while you watched your own father buried through a telephone screen at your kitchen table.

Maybe it was your church, chained shut on Easter Sunday while the state government announced that the liquor store and the casino could remain open for business. I sued over exactly that, because congregations were treated as a public menace while gambling halls ran all night.

Maybe it was your children — two years staring at a laptop, a child who now reads two grades behind, a graduation year that simply never happened, and a teenager who has never really been the same since.

Maybe it was your mother in the nursing home. Ten months of waving at her through a window, and near the end she no longer knew who was waving.

You did all of it. You closed up your business, you stayed inside your home, and you buried people alone, because you were repeatedly assured that there was no alternative.

Now here is what that man was doing while you obeyed.

Senator Rand Paul released 1,100 pages of Anthony Fauci's private diary. In his own words, written at the time, Fauci kept "an open mind about the possibility of a lab leak" — while publicly branding that same idea a conspiracy theory and smearing anyone who dared to raise it. People like you. People like me.

So while you sat in that parking lot, the man giving the orders privately had his doubts, and he simply never shared a single one of them with you.

Then, on July 29 of this year, the Senate finally subpoenaed him. He raised his right hand and took the Fifth Amendment. Not once, and not twice. He took it 111 times.

You gave up two years of your life on his word. He would not give thirty seconds of honest testimony on yours. That is not science. That is contempt for you.

And let me be blunt, because I have never been anything else. This man is not a scientist who made an honest mistake. He is a criminal who ran a cover-up, and the wreckage of your business, your church and your family was the price of it. Innocent men do not take the Fifth 111 times.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzZ9AAwAAAAAAoChvBstsBblRqf-zIjNSJPiMy0YUaAbbCCv57M59bLFXi6szeMHuSJTDI5XoUR2YzDQM5giZrXraiVvrV43O_D_lPwv70Eqw4Q5yEAYKQ
Stand with me and help fund this case.

My name is Larry Klayman. I founded Judicial Watch, I served as a federal prosecutor, and in more than 40 years of legal warfare I became the only lawyer in American history to have a court rule that a sitting president committed a crime.

Today I run Freedom Watch, and we have something the Senate does not: an active federal lawsuit in Dallas, Texas over COVID-19. We filed it in March 2020 against the Chinese Communist Party and its Wuhan lab, seeking trillions in damages for a nationwide class of victims, and that class could include you.

I am now amending that complaint to add Anthony Fauci as a defendant, along with former so-called President Joe Biden, to invalidate the phony and illegal pardon that the Biden Crime Family slipped him in the dead of night. That question could go all the way to the Supreme Court, and this case may be the only vehicle to take it there.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzZ9AAwAAAAAAoChvBsuh7xBlWdEe9ipdcGWGVmCdTGdhnYsLKf1QHk1M8qC2raTKiaC4jBATy47oQ8SfNBZKo4EKhQUjwkql92exnXaDNoSMlZVIUM5zg
Fund the amended complaint against Fauci and Biden.

"But didn't Biden pardon him?"

A pardon is no defense to a civil lawsuit. It stops a prosecutor, and nothing more. It cannot stop a jury from ordering Fauci to pay damages for what he did. In my courtroom that pardon is a worthless scrap of paper.

And that midnight pardon has a problem of its own. The House Oversight Committee found that Biden's last-minute pardons were signed by autopen — by a machine — with no proof that Biden even knew about them, and declared them null and void. The Supreme Court said more than a century ago that accepting a pardon carries "a confession" of guilt. So we will ask the court to strike that pardon down, and we will go after Joe Biden for issuing it.

Better still, a jury in a civil case is allowed by binding Supreme Court precedent to hold a defendant's silence against him as evidence that he is liable. He handed us Exhibit A, 111 times over.

Senator Paul says he will hold a contempt vote, and God bless him for trying. But you and I both know exactly how that ends: the filibuster will kill it, and official Washington will protect its own. The Senate has not successfully held anyone in contempt since 1971.

That is why Freedom Watch exists. We are your real Justice Department — because the one in Washington has been inert, and the Senate is a debating society with a coat check.

Congressional hearings produce headlines and press releases, while federal lawsuits produce subpoenas, sworn testimony, documentary evidence and enforceable judgments. Missouri already won a $24 billion judgment against China over COVID and is moving to seize Chinese assets to collect it, so do not tell me this cannot be done.

But a fight of this size is WAR, and war costs money. Freedom Watch is a 501(c)(3), your gift is tax-deductible, and every dollar goes straight into this case.

Give $25, $50, $100 or more right now.

You gave them two years, and they never asked. I am asking. Give me one gift, and I will haul these people into court and get you the answers they owe you.

In Justice,Larry KlaymanFounder, Judicial Watch and Freedom WatchChairman and General Counsel, Freedom Watch, Inc.

And his private diary says he had doubts the whole time. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Dear Patriot, Do you remember when it was only fifteen days? Fifteen days to slow the spread. That was the promise they made you, and you believed it, because a doctor on television told you that the science demanded it and you are a decent person who did not want to hurt anybody. Do you remember what your street sounded like that spring? Nothing at all — no traffic, no children playing outside, no church bells on Sunday morning. Only sirens, running all day and into the night, and the sound of your own television counting the dead. Do you remember the plywood going up over the storefronts downtown? The caution tape wrapped around the swing sets? The arrows taped to the floor of the grocery store, and the man who shouted at you for standing too close to him in the aisle? Fifteen days eventually became two years. So let me ask you the question that nobody in Washington has ever bothered to ask you. What did those two years take from you? Not from the country. From you. Help me get you the answer, under oath. Maybe it was the business — thirty years of your life invested in it, and then a paper sign taped to the glass. The big chain store down the road stayed open and sold the very same goods, because yours was ruled "non-essential." Some of you never opened those doors again. Maybe it was your father's funeral, with only ten mourners permitted, while you watched your own father buried through a telephone screen at your kitchen table. Maybe it was your church, chained shut on Easter Sunday while the state government announced that the liquor store and the casino could remain open for business. I sued over exactly that, because congregations were treated as a public menace while gambling halls ran all night. Maybe it was your children — two years staring at a laptop, a child who now reads two grades behind, a graduation year that simply never happened, and a teenager who has never really been the same since. Maybe it was your mother in the nursing home. Ten months of waving at her through a window, and near the end she no longer knew who was waving. You did all of it. You closed up your business, you stayed inside your home, and you buried people alone, because you were repeatedly assured that there was no alternative. Now here is what that man was doing while you obeyed. Senator Rand Paul released 1,100 pages of Anthony Fauci's private diary. In his own words, written at the time, Fauci kept "an open mind about the possibility of a lab leak" — while publicly branding that same idea a conspiracy theory and smearing anyone who dared to raise it. People like you. People like me. So while you sat in that parking lot, the man giving the orders privately had his doubts, and he simply never shared a single one of them with you. GIVE $25, $50 OR $100 — MAKE HIM EXPLAIN IT UNDER OATH $25 $50 $100 OTHER Then, on July 29 of this year, the Senate finally subpoenaed him. He raised his right hand and took the Fifth Amendment. Not once, and not twice. He took it 111 times. You gave up two years of your life on his word. He would not give thirty seconds of honest testimony on yours. That is not science. That is contempt for you. And let me be blunt, because I have never been anything else. This man is not a scientist who made an honest mistake. He is a criminal who ran a cover-up, and the wreckage of your business, your church and your family was the price of it. Innocent men do not take the Fifth 111 times. Stand with me and help fund this case. My name is Larry Klayman. I founded Judicial Watch, I served as a federal prosecutor, and in more than 40 years of legal warfare I became the only lawyer in American history to have a court rule that a sitting president committed a crime. Today I run Freedom Watch, and we have something the Senate does not: an active federal lawsuit in Dallas, Texas over COVID-19. We filed it in March 2020 against the Chinese Communist Party and its Wuhan lab, seeking trillions in damages for a nationwide class of victims, and that class could include you. I am now amending that complaint to add Anthony Fauci as a defendant, along with former so-called President Joe Biden, to invalidate the phony and illegal pardon that the Biden Crime Family slipped him in the dead of night. That question could go all the way to the Supreme Court, and this case may be the only vehicle to take it there. Fund the amended complaint against Fauci and Biden. "But didn't Biden pardon him?" A pardon is no defense to a civil lawsuit. It stops a prosecutor, and nothing more. It cannot stop a jury from ordering Fauci to pay damages for what he did. In my courtroom that pardon is a worthless scrap of paper. And that midnight pardon has a problem of its own. The House Oversight Committee found that Biden's last-minute pardons were signed by autopen — by a machine — with no proof that Biden even knew about them, and declared them null and void. The Supreme Court said more than a century ago that accepting a pardon carries "a confession" of guilt. So we will ask the court to strike that pardon down, and we will go after Joe Biden for issuing it. Better still, a jury in a civil case is allowed by binding Supreme Court precedent to hold a defendant's silence against him as evidence that he is liable. He handed us Exhibit A, 111 times over. Senator Paul says he will hold a contempt vote, and God bless him for trying. But you and I both know exactly how that ends: the filibuster will kill it, and official Washington will protect its own. The Senate has not successfully held anyone in contempt since 1971. That is why Freedom Watch exists. We are your real Justice Department — because the one in Washington has been inert, and the Senate is a debating society with a coat check. Congressional hearings produce headlines and press releases, while federal lawsuits produce subpoenas, sworn testimony, documentary evidence and enforceable judgments. Missouri already won a $24 billion judgment against China over COVID and is moving to seize Chinese assets to collect it, so do not tell me this cannot be done. But a fight of this size is WAR, and war costs money. Freedom Watch is a 501(c)(3), your gift is tax-deductible, and every dollar goes straight into this case. Give $25, $50, $100 or more right now. You gave them two years, and they never asked. I am asking. Give me one gift, and I will haul these people into court and get you the answers they owe you. In Justice,Larry KlaymanFounder, Judicial Watch and Freedom WatchChairman and General Counsel, Freedom Watch, Inc. P.S. You lost a business, a funeral, a church, or two years of your child's life — and he took the Fifth 111 times rather than tell you why. In civil court, that silence can be used against him. We file within weeks, and I want your name standing with mine when we do. RUSH YOUR GIFT BEFORE WE FILE $25 $50 $100 OTHER

subject: My full name
